Guide to This Supplement

This supplement accompanies The Unification of Matter, Forces, and Spacetime from the Bost–Connes System; together they constitute the rewritten manuscript. The main paper presents the physical relations, core formulas, and conditions under which they hold. This supplement retains the complete dependency index and provides the corresponding detailed dynamical proofs.

Section, equation, and theorem numbers prefixed by S refer to this supplement; all other chapter, section, and equation numbers refer to the accompanying main paper. Reference numbers follow the main paper. Q numbers identify dependency items. Conditional constructions, established consequences, and physical identifications are stated within the scope of each item.

This supplement follows the physical sequence of the main paper, placing constructions shared by later proofs first. S1–S3 develop the thermal cycle, formation phase, and convergence. S4–S7 establish records and nodes, spectral references, common-source participation, and the common matter–background carrier. S8 proves the normalization preservation used in resonance corrections; S9 and S10 treat metric processes with persistent replenishment and with complete spatial round trips, respectively. S11–S14 then give the specific proofs for the nucleon scale, up-type return, neutrino mass matrix, and nucleon phase. S15 gives the joint representation of quantum attributes and conditional selection by weak contact. S16 connects formation records, node visits, and actual returns into common persistent down-type and up-type processes, and proves their motion and common-source background response. Each proof retains its actual preparations, operations, and scope of readings. Specific examples cited ahead of their main treatment remain grouped with the corresponding physical objects.

Q01–Q22 summarize model inputs, constructed results, physical identifications, and their scope by function, for cross-chapter reference. A single item may contain content of these different kinds; the numbers identify dependency items, not the number of independent parameters or unproved propositions. Specific constructions and proofs are listed in the last column.

Masses expressed on the vv scale share Q06 and Q07; weak occupation and the remaining background are realized by the outputs from a common source in 6.1.2. Results that additionally invoke corrected couplings inherit the corresponding conditions listed in Q10. Subsequent uses of these results inherit their specified preparation, action, and calibration; paths and readouts added for each family are listed under the corresponding items.

S1 Cycle with fixed thermal preparation

This section retains the original cycle of fixed thermal preparation, coherent retrieval, and shell-average restoration. Its thermalization conclusion follows §4.4 of Ref. 2. Coherent delivery and persistent protection in Chapter 2 of the main text do not automatically satisfy the restoration structure of this section; the isospectral temporary storage in 4.4.3 separately preserves and returns the carrier.

S1.1 Complete cycle

Using the joint unitary action 𝕌 and environment preparation ηℰη_{ℰ} from 2.3.1, denote the projections onto the shell-average subspace 𝒞 and the direction space ℳ by Π and P, respectively. The shell-preserving input control V is the identity on the shell-average subspace, preserves the direction space, and commutes with HKH_{K}. The fixed restoration preparation is

σgsh=∑j=0Kgj|ej⟩⟨ej|,gj>0,∑jgj=1.\sigma_g^{\mathrm{sh}}=\sum_{j=0}^{K}g_j|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|,\qquad g_j>0,\quad\sum_jg_j=1.(S1)

Preparing the environment independently in each cycle and taking the partial trace of the complete output gives the cycle 𝓕V,g𝓕_{V,g} in the main text 7, 8. The following calculation allows background–direction coherence in the initial state; decomposition according to the actual output is performed only after restoration.

S1.2 Formation, decay, and retrieval

Take a direction ν, background endpoint eae_{a}, and their shell energies EνE_{ν} and EaE_{a}. We calculate below the coefficients of the exchange and restoration specified in 2.3.1.

In the specified channel, choose thermal environment states u and v such that the joint vectors |ν,u⟩ and |ea,v⟩\vert e_{a},v\rangle have the same total energy and total unit-group charge. The exchange angle αaνα_{aν} determines the rotation between them:

Waν|ν,u⟩=cos⁡αaν|ν,u⟩+sin⁡αaν|ea,v⟩,Waν|ea,v⟩=cos⁡αaν|ea,v⟩−sin⁡αaν|ν,u⟩.W_{a\nu}|\nu,u\rangle=\cos\alpha_{a\nu}|\nu,u\rangle+\sin\alpha_{a\nu}|e_a,v\rangle,\qquad W_{a\nu}|e_a,v\rangle=\cos\alpha_{a\nu}|e_a,v\rangle-\sin\alpha_{a\nu}|\nu,u\rangle.(S2)

The component remaining in the direction space is then coherently retrieved through the zero element. Write z=|0⟩. Prepare the retrieval auxiliary in g, and associate direction ν with auxiliary state aνa_{ν}; g and all aνa_{ν} form an orthonormal set. The round trip temporarily stores the direction coefficients in the same auxiliary system and then returns them with phase wνw_{ν}:

|ν,g⟩↦wν|z,aν⟩↦wν|ν,g⟩,|wν|=1.|\nu,g\rangle\longmapsto w_\nu|z,a_\nu\rangle\longmapsto w_\nu|\nu,g\rangle,\qquad |w_\nu|=1.(S3)

The same auxiliary is retained throughout the round trip and is restored to the common g at the endpoint. Including free evolution, denote the net cycle phase of each direction by φνφ_{ν}, represented in the reduced cycle by Uφ=Π+∑νeiφνPνU_{φ}=Π+\sum _{ν} e^{iφ_{ν}}P_{ν}. Relative phases between different directions are calculated from this complete action.

The component transferred into the shell-average subspace is restored according to the prescribed preparation. Introduce auxiliary labels rjar_{ja} that are jointly orthonormal in both indices and orthogonal to g and all aνa_{ν}. For input eae_{a}, the restoration acts as follows:

|ea,g⟩↦|Ya⟩=∑j=0Kgj|ej,rja⟩,Tr⁡R|Ya⟩⟨Yb|=δabσgsh,Tr⁡R(|ν,g⟩⟨Ya|)=0.|e_a,g\rangle\longmapsto |Y_a\rangle=\sum_{j=0}^{K}\sqrt{g_j}\,|e_j,r_{ja}\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_R|Y_a\rangle\langle Y_b|=\delta_{ab}\sigma_g^{\mathrm{sh}},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_R\!\left(|\nu,g\rangle\langle Y_a|\right)=0.(S4)

Orthogonality in both indices gives the latter two equations: a background input is restored to σgshσ_{g}^{\mathrm{sh}}, background–direction cross terms vanish under the partial trace, and returned directions remain unchanged. The distinctions between the input and shell labels remain in the joint state; auxiliary state g and share gjg_{j} are defined separately.

S1.3 Formation shares and uninterrupted maintenance

Formation and decay shares in the same exchange are determined by the channel preparation and exchange angle. For the selected channel, let the preparation shares be aaν>0a_{aν}>0 and 0<αaν<π/20<α_{aν}<π/2; the unexchanged preparation has share a0=1−∑aaν>0a_{0}=1-\sum a_{aν}>0. Put Δaν=Ea−EνΔ_{aν}=E_{a}-E_{ν}. The thermal-block shares on u and v satisfy

tu=11+eβΔaν,tv=eβΔaν1+eβΔaν,tu+tv=1.t_u=\frac1{1+e^{\beta\Delta_{a\nu}}},\qquad t_v=\frac{e^{\beta\Delta_{a\nu}}}{1+e^{\beta\Delta_{a\nu}}},\qquad t_u+t_v=1.(S5)

Multiplying the preparation shares by the squared moduli of the corresponding transfer amplitudes gives exit share εaνε_{aν} and formation share fνaf_{νa}:

ϵaν=aaνtusin⁡2αaν,fνa=aaνtvsin⁡2αaν,ϵaνfνa=e−β(Ea−Eν).\epsilon_{a\nu}=a_{a\nu}t_u\sin^2\alpha_{a\nu},\qquad f_{\nu a}=a_{a\nu}t_v\sin^2\alpha_{a\nu},\qquad \frac{\epsilon_{a\nu}}{f_{\nu a}}=e^{-\beta(E_a-E_\nu)}.(S6)

The ratio formula applies to the selected positive exchange channels at finite β; both shares are set to zero for unselected channels. Thermal preparation fixes the ratio between forward and reverse shares, while the exchange angle and channel-preparation shares determine their absolute sizes. Summing for the same input, write ϵν=∑aϵaν\epsilon_\nu=\sum_a\epsilon_{a\nu} and ka=1−∑νfνak_a=1-\sum_\nu f_{\nu a}. Without input control, the system outputs of the complete cycle for the two inputs are

ℱI,g(Pν)=(1−ϵν)Pν+ϵνσgsh,ℱI,g(Pea)=∑νfνaPν+kaσgsh.\mathcal F_{I,g}(P_\nu)=(1-\epsilon_\nu)P_\nu+\epsilon_\nu\sigma_g^{\mathrm{sh}},\qquad \mathcal F_{I,g}(P_{e_a})=\sum_\nu f_{\nu a}P_\nu+k_a\sigma_g^{\mathrm{sh}}.(S7)

The two equations give survival of the original direction and new formation from the background, respectively; the system state obtained by summing over the formation channels is generally mixed.

For a direction input X=PXP, the non-exit subchannel 𝒬V(X)=P𝓕V,g(X)P𝒬_{V}(X)=P𝓕_{V,g}(X)P is completely positive and trace-nonincreasing. Pattern preservation for normalized ψ, with Pψ=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|P_{ψ}=\vert ψ\rangle \langle ψ\vert, requires

𝒬V(Pψ)=sψPψ,sψ=Tr⁡𝒬V(Pψ)>0.\mathcal Q_V(P_\psi)=s_\psi P_\psi,\qquad s_\psi=\operatorname{Tr}\mathcal Q_V(P_\psi)>0.(S8)

Starting from a normalized direction state ρ₀, Tr⁡𝒬Vn(ρ0)\operatorname{Tr}𝒬_{V}^{n}(ρ_{0}) gives the share surviving n consecutive cycles without exit. In particular, a single uncontrolled direction satisfies

𝒬In(Pν)=(1−ϵν)nPν,sn=(1−ϵν)n.\mathcal Q_I^n(P_\nu)=(1-\epsilon_\nu)^nP_\nu,\qquad s_n=(1-\epsilon_\nu)^n.(S9)

This formula allows pattern preservation with a finite lifetime; components newly formed after an exit are not counted as uninterrupted survival.

For a general initial state, after first-cycle restoration and the partial trace over the environment, the system state has the form ρn=Xn+ynσgsh\rho_n=X_n+y_n\sigma_g^{\mathrm{sh}}, where Xn=PXnP≥0X_n=PX_nP\ge0, Tr⁡Xn+yn=1\operatorname{Tr}X_n+y_n=1, and n≥1n\ge1. The original cycle in S1 uses shell energy HKH_{K} and fixed environment energy HℰH_{ℰ}. If another phase generator is also to serve as the conserved energy in the same exchange, it must satisfy the following restriction. Under the strict-contraction conditions of §4.4 in Ref. 2, fix the same complete joint unitary action 𝕌 and environment energy HℰH_{ℰ}, using the same energy unit. If this energy also generates the cycle phase being read, its actual unwrapped value must satisfy −φ̃ν/τ=Eν+κE-\widetilde{φ}_{ν}/τ=E_{ν}+κ_{E}; at the cycle endpoints, this requires wν=e−iτκEw_{ν}=e^{-iτκ_{E}} to be the same for every direction. Under the fixed complete exchange, environment energy, and strict-contraction conditions above, directions in the same shell have the same conserved energy. Distinct mass phases within a shell therefore require a separately established compatible joint dynamics if they are to represent exchange energy differences.

The unit-action identification remains a condition linking the process to spectral evaluation. The actual return continuously feeds the mean of the input block into the phase; for an unprotected bare spectral auxiliary, the mean of a matrix exponential generally cannot be replaced by the exponential of the mean.

S3.3 Survival envelope and spectral separation

Take the actual survival share 0<qT≤10<q_T\le1. Thermal reconnection uses target transport and filtering that act as the identity on the source, auxiliaries, and logical degrees of freedom not participating in this action, and compensates the free unitary over the entire transient domain. Each successful fine branch is rηI\sqrt{r_\eta}I, and the complementary output effects sum to (1−qT)I(1-q_T)I. The survival subchannel is then exactly ℒ=qTℱ\mathcal L=q_T\mathcal F, with exit effect (1−qT)I(1-q_T)I. Cycle-by-cycle composition gives the survival and first-exit formulas of the main text; source- or mode-dependent filtering does not satisfy this premise.

Formation transients can also be spectrally separated from coherence within the code. The interaction-picture limit above defines a completely positive trace-preserving map Π\Pi satisfying Π𝒥=Id\Pi\mathcal J=\mathrm{Id} and Πℱ=Ad⁡UΠ\Pi\mathcal F=\operatorname{Ad}_U\Pi, where 𝒥(σ)=𝒥sσ𝒥s†\mathcal J(\sigma)=\mathcal J_s\sigma\mathcal J_s^\dagger. If h|a⟩=Ea|a⟩h|a\rangle=E_a|a\rangle, then

This includes the degeneracy multiplicities of coherence within the code, while giving only a radius bound for the remaining spectrum. The map Π\Pi is a mathematical asymptotic readout, not an additional measurement; the infinite-cycle result uses the reduced limit with a continuing supply of fresh auxiliaries and environments. When qT<1q_T<1, the unnormalized survival share ultimately tends to zero, while the orbit conditioned on survival still satisfies the proved bound. Visible spectral lines also depend on input and readout overlaps; no specific decay products or lifetimes are obtained here.

The selected serial cycle period is τ=tH+TR+TX\tau=t_H+T_R+T_X: TRT_R includes readiness, auxiliary replacement, forward and inverse spectral operations, and feedback; TXT_X includes thermal transport, filtering, compensation, and routing. Formation auxiliary units restored to the same preparation along every fine record can be reused across cycles; retrieval auxiliaries are restored on survival and leave with the information-carrying output at first exit. Initial loading counts as startup; fresh thermal baths, pointers, and unrestored auxiliaries must still be supplied.

S4 Records, nodes, and coherent return

This section supplies the record conditions required by the path rules in the main text and calculates nodes and whole-group projections at general depth and for a general background amplitude ratio.

S4.1 Records and conditional outputs

Actual records must be distinguished by orthogonal pointers and remain in the complete output through retrieval, reconstruction, and the retention period under discussion. The zero-element round trip in S1 restores the auxiliary to the common state g, so the intermediately distinguishable aνa_{ν} are not terminal records. Distinguishing return, decay, formation, and background continuation also requires retention of the input class; a terminal label alone does not distinguish all these processes.

Fix the same final system state, with path amplitudes AαA_{α} and normalized final environment states εαε_{α}. The squared norm of the complete output gives

w=∑α,α′AαAα′¯⟨εα′|εα⟩.w=\sum_{\alpha,\alpha'}A_\alpha\overline{A_{\alpha'}}\langle\varepsilon_{\alpha'}|\varepsilon_\alpha\rangle.(S26)

For complete pointer projections {Πr}\{Π_{r}\}, including the no-response outcome, write v=∑αAαεαv=\sum_\alpha A_\alpha\varepsilon_\alpha. The shares wr=∥Πrv∥2w_r=\|\Pi_rv\|^2 then satisfy ∑rwr=∥v∥2=w\sum_rw_r=\|v\|^2=w. If complete final states of paths in the same class are εα=eiϕαεr\varepsilon_\alpha=e^{i\phi_\alpha}\varepsilon_r, with distinct r orthogonal, only after absorbing Aα←AαeiϕαA_\alpha\leftarrow A_\alpha e^{i\phi_\alpha} do we obtain w=∑r|∑α∈rAα|2w=\sum_r|\sum_{\alpha\in r}A_\alpha|^2. Merely merging pointer names does not change environment inner products; mixed preparations require a separate sum over preparation weights.

Under statistical conditions (F0)–(F4) 2, the joint final state ΩoutΩ_{\mathrm{out}} including detection gives pr=Tr⁡[(I⊗Πr)Ωout]p_r=\operatorname{Tr}[(I\otimes\Pi_r)\Omega_{\mathrm{out}}]. When outcome r occurs and pr>0p_{r}>0, the unnormalized conditional state must be divided by prp_{r}; orthogonal records do not guarantee statistical independence of earlier and later stages, whose composition still uses the complete instrument of 2.4.2. Selected records may be separated by many cycles; no-response cycles must still be counted in both statistics and elapsed duration.

Internal-state identification in 9.1.2 is also tested by actual measurement. For normalized states σA\sigma_A and σC\sigma_C, perfect single-shot discrimination within the unrestricted measurement class is possible if and only if their supports are orthogonal. If 0≤E≤I0\le E\le I has probabilities 1 and 0 on the two states, positivity forces their supports into the eigenvalue-1 space and kernel of E, respectively, so they are orthogonal; conversely, the support projection of σA\sigma_A distinguishes two preparations with orthogonal supports. A restricted instrument must additionally implement this deterministic discrimination.

For a pure joint output ∑aca|a⟩|ea⟩\sum_a c_a|a\rangle|e_a\rangle, with orthonormal system basis |a⟩|a\rangle and normalized environment vectors |ea⟩|e_a\rangle, the reduced matrix entries are ρab=cac‾b⟨eb|ea⟩\rho_{ab}=c_a\bar c_b\langle e_b|e_a\rangle: occupations use squared moduli, while coherences also contain environment overlaps. Restoration in S1 removes background–direction coherence from the system; the associated phases must be read before restoration or through a joint readout of the still-accessible environment.

S4.2 Node overlaps

We use the normalization rules of 2.4.3 and 3.3: an equal-amplitude orbit of h points has single-point amplitude 1/√h and share 1/h, where h must be the actual orbit size. Multiplication of CRT overlaps requires product preparation and product readout. The following calculations distinguish a single point, a single deep-layer point pair, and a complete species group.

Write N=φ(pᴷ) and e0=N−1/2∑u∈S0|u⟩e_{0}=N^{-1/2}\sum _{u∈S_{0}}\vert u\rangle. For D={u,−u}D=\{u,-u\}, put dD±=(|u⟩±|−u⟩)/2d_D^\pm=(|u\rangle\pm|-u\rangle)/\sqrt2 and let QDQ_{D} be the projection onto this point pair. Then

S4.4 Returnable routes and permanent records

Species directions, vacuum-counting addresses, and propagation wave numbers specify the formation pattern, participating preparation, and propagation eigendirections, respectively. Group-element and character descriptions of a factor can be interchanged only after establishing a concrete Fourier transform on the same group and representation. A species pattern at zero propagation wave number does not eliminate the matter’s logical position register. All records below belong to the complete joint state; not reading a record does not erase it.

Suppose two paths give system vectors a,ba,b, with complete final auxiliary states Ra,RbR_a,R_b. After tracing out the auxiliaries, the cross block is |a⟩⟨b|⟨Rb|Ra⟩|a\rangle\langle b|\langle R_b|R_a\rangle. Orthogonal terminal records make it vanish; a common unitary inverse that restores auxiliaries to a shared ready state can preserve it. This criterion applies to addresses, paths, and exit times, but labels of these three distinct factors cannot simply be identified as one record.

S5.3 Finite truncation and tail bounds

For β>1, monotonicity of n⁻ᵝ and integral comparison give

ZL(β)→ζ(β),0<ζ(β)−ZL(β)<∫L∞x−βdx=L1−ββ−1(β>1).Z_L(\beta)\longrightarrow\zeta(\beta),\qquad 0<\zeta(\beta)-Z_L(\beta)<\int_L^\infty x^{-\beta}\,dx=\frac{L^{1-\beta}}{\beta-1}\quad(\beta>1).(S49)

Nontrivial character sums contain phases and are not traces of positive operators. The full-space b accumulates all integer terms, whereas the trivial unit-group character excludes multiples of p, giving responses ζ(β) and (1−p⁻ᵝ)ζ(β), respectively, in the convergence domain. Their physical connections to positive spectral participation all use the reference and matching conditions specified in the main text.

S6 Common-source participation and common frequency

This section first obtains participation outputs from the same occupation process, then constructs the return columns and common frequency. Configuration formation uses this return construction, and its complete matching subsequently enters the collective column.

S6.1 Common-source occupation and matching preservation

Assumptions. In a finite joint state space, the process participation projection is P4P_4 of rank N0N_0, and the orthogonal reference-background projection is PbrefP_b^{\mathrm{ref}} of rank MM. The reduced input address state is (P4+Pbref)/Z0(P_4+P_b^{\mathrm{ref}})/Z_0, with Z0=N0+MZ_0=N_0+M. If a finite thermal preparation approximates it, its preparation error must be retained separately; a finite number of cycles cannot automatically be called an exact stationary state. We use role encoding within the same P4P_4, compatible with joint energy and group charge: PBP_B has rank 18 and Pr≤PBP_r\le P_B has rank 3; P2,P3≤P4−PBP_2,P_3\le P_4-P_B have ranks 1 and 2, respectively, and are orthogonal. Identifying the neutral-register representation of the eighteen labels with these address roles is an adopted encoding condition.

The three fixed probes of the original complete spectral instrument give success weights wi∈[0,1]w_i\in[0,1], using the verified unit capacity. The initial occupation is PBP_B; PrP_r is released when the first type of spectral probe succeeds, while P2,P3P_2,P_3 are added on their respective spectral successes. Success controls only the occupation bit, without transporting addresses, and all original spectral-failure and auxiliary records are retained. Occupation is read after a single preparation; repeated attempts use actual repreparation, rather than repeatedly applying XOR to the old occupation bit.

Theorem S6.1 (Common-source outputs and the maximal matching-preserving space). The actual process above yields three unnormalized address outputs: occupation, process remainder, and reference background,

BW=PB−w1Pr+w2P2+w3P3,0≤BW≤P4,ΓW=BW/Z0,Γvac=(P4−BW)/Z0,Γb=Pbref/Z0.\begin{gathered} B_W=P_B-w_1P_r+w_2P_2+w_3P_3,\qquad 0\le B_W\le P_4,\\ \boxed{\Gamma_W=B_W/Z_0,\quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}=(P_4-B_W)/Z_0,\quad \Gamma_b=P_b^{\mathrm{ref}}/Z_0.} \end{gathered}(S50)

The coefficients sum to 1 and all failures have been counted.

Take the initial state as the uniform coherent vector on AA, namely state v=0v=0 in the Fourier basis. The action ZwZ_w shifts the Fourier index by ww, so evolution remains in sector II and becomes the finite random walk with the edge-difference steps above. Each coefficient in the spanning-tree basis can be reached with at most p−1p-1 forward steps; reversing an edge of the spanning tree realizes a negative step in p−1p-1 steps. Full support is therefore reached by step (p−1)(n−1)(p-1)(n-1) at the latest, with idle branches padding the cycle count. Full support here does not mean uniformity after finitely many cycles.

This random walk is irreducible on the index set and has a positive holding probability, so its unique stationary distribution is uniform. Its Fourier eigenvalues and the purity for the specified initial state are

Proof: characters diagonalize translation convolution on the finite abelian group II. Parseval’s identity gives the purity formula. It applies to the initial state and actual channel used here, not as a finite-cycle matching formula for arbitrary nonuniform or correlated preparations. Other total-sum sectors are not attracted into II by this channel. If all probes and comparison actions are completely reversed, the initial state is restored; the reduced formation above cannot simultaneously be claimed to remain.

Likewise, for a fixed observable XX of a random-unitary channel with positive weights, strict convexity of the Hilbert–Schmidt norm gives [X,Zwsg]=0[X,Z_{w_{sg}}]=0: equality of norms requires all conjugated XX to coincide, and the idle branch fixes them to XX. This criterion identifies which structure remains preserved by actual observation after the partial trace.

Formation supplies the configuration set, complete comparison gives the event effect, and the actual collective column of S6.5 gives the frequency; each step uses its own explicit preparation and complete operation.

S8.1 Actual terminal action and stability

Use neutral, equal-energy three-state terminal records, with the complete self-adjoint action

More generally, define S=E++E−S=E_++E_- and ΔL=∑n=0L−1Tn(Δ)\Delta_L=\sum_{n=0}^{L-1}T^n(\Delta). This bound does not grow with the number of retries and does not require a uniform positive lower bound on the delivery probability. It controls relative exit imbalance; an absolute error bound unrelated to SS alone cannot give this guarantee at low delivery probabilities.

The terminal Hamiltonian above gives a complete conditional realization of balanced exits. The static generator of 7.3.2 in the main text gives D=x2/(x+y)D=x^2/(x+y) but does not itself specify these two terminal projections. To connect the results as the same original process, one must still calculate E±=Jin†U†Π±UJinE_\pm=J_{\mathrm{in}}^\dagger U^\dagger\Pi_\pm UJ_{\mathrm{in}} using its actual joint unitary UU, input isometric column JinJ_{\mathrm{in}}, and actual exits Π±\Pi_\pm, then test yE+=xE−yE_+=xE_- and the connection conditions for the fixed auxiliary preparation and its filtering. Average balance for just one preparation and one cutoff does not prove the operator identity for all inputs. The theorem already includes any common continuation subchannel required for normalization preservation, without additionally requiring scalar restoration each cycle; the correspondence between the original virtual process and the actual exits still has to be established.

S9 Matter sources, background propagation, and metric strength

This section first establishes delivery of the positive source, then distinguishes position propagation in the original thermal cycle from persistent replenishment of resource units. Each is calculated from its own complete procedure; the subsequent metric strength uses the explicitly specified resource return and timing.

Position occupation probabilities need not evolve autonomously. Select only the terminal thermal edges from directions to the zero element. pn+1=𝖠pn+𝖡𝖣nh0+∑k=0n−1𝖡𝖣n−1−k𝖢pk,pn=𝒟ρn,hn=𝒬ρn.p_{n+1}=\mathsf A p_n+\mathsf B\mathsf D^nh_0 +\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\mathsf B\mathsf D^{n-1-k}\mathsf C p_k, \quad p_n=\mathcal D\rho_n,\quad h_n=\mathcal Q\rho_n.(S110)

Occupation-probability evolution is strictly autonomous for every input if and only if 𝖡=0\mathsf B=0; even when restricted to diagonal initial states, 𝖡𝖣k𝖢\mathsf B\mathsf D^k\mathsf C must be checked. This memory comes from system coherence and does not require the old environment to participate again.

This gives complete results for propagation and relaxation in the original thermal cycle. To use it for metric-background propagation, the change in the joint state induced by a matter source and the test maintenance phase must additionally be connected to the same channel, with a correspondence for spatial scales. The resource-return coefficient of S9 comes from its explicit source-writing and testing protocol and cannot be replaced by ℛ\mathscr R without this step.

S9.4 Thermal survival and persistent replenishment

Let s,ts,t denote the distinct resource units associated with the source and test, respectively. Each component of resource configuration 𝒏\mathbf n takes value 0 or 1; EtE_t refreshes the test resource unit to an unbiased preparation, while Es(b)E_s(b) replaces the source resource unit by a preparation of occupation probability 1/2+b1/2+b, retaining all other resource units. The actual transport and unbiased boundary update is ℛ\mathcal R, with first moment I−cLI-cL, where L>0L>0 is the Laplacian of the finite Dirichlet resource graph. Use the edgewise exchange rule of the main text so that weights are nonnegative; for example, each edge has probability cc and the total edge weight is at most 1/21/2. Each cycle selects no contact, test contact, or source contact with probabilities 1−2ε,ε,ε1-2\varepsilon,\varepsilon,\varepsilon, where 0<ε<1/20<\varepsilon<1/2. The complete configuration coherence block is

Dt(z)=diag⁡𝒏e−2iz(1−nt),Tb(z)=ℛ[(1−2ε)Dt(z)+εEtDt(z)Et+εEs(b)Dt(z)],T0(z)=Tb(z)|b=0.\begin{aligned} D_t(z)&=\operatorname{diag}_{\mathbf n}e^{-2iz(1-n_t)},\\ T_b(z)&=\mathcal R\big[(1-2\varepsilon)D_t(z) +\varepsilon E_tD_t(z)E_t+\varepsilon E_s(b)D_t(z)\big],\\ T_0(z)&=T_b(z)\big|_{b=0}. \end{aligned}(S111)

Records of the original resource units are not ignored; they are summed within the complete refreshing channel. When the source is absent, source contact is still performed using an unbiased preparation; turning off that contact requires recalculating the return kernel.

After source activity, execute the thermal instrument transported from 2.3.5 of the main text to the positive-source code subspace, with survival and exit effects qTIq_T I and (1−qT)I(1-q_T)I. Exit outputs are moved out and retained, and the vacancy is restored to the same loading entrance; replenishment follows S9.1 at cycle end. Thermal and preparation windows act as the identity on resources, the test, and their correlations, and the complete delivery effect is fIfI. With a ready entrance and all steps included, f=QMf=Q_M. Multiple attempts alone do not justify f=1−(1−q)Mf=1-(1-q)^M; that formula additionally requires independent restoration after failure and complete preservation after success.

S9.8 Averaging limit of passive maintenance

This section proves the averaging window used in 4.4.2 of the main paper for the passive resource–carrier channel of 4.3; resource transfer is independent of the test state and cannot be replaced by the active two-contact process. All constants below refer to the same fixed finite mixing resource process, whose mixing rate is not changed when taking the small-accumulation limit.

Fix a finite mixing resource process and its stationary distribution πb\pi_b, and put K𝒏=ηB𝒏K_{\mathbf n}=\eta B_{\mathbf n}, where B𝒏B_{\mathbf n} remains bounded and η\eta is the small accumulation per cycle. Write aH=ηAHa_H=\eta A_H and ax=ηAxa_x=\eta A_x. Starting from the stationary product entrance ρ𝒏=πb(𝒏)ρ\rho_{\mathbf n}=\pi_b(\mathbf n)\rho, resource updates preserve this entrance distribution. Expanding the active unitary of the main paper’s resource–carrier channel to first order gives

∑𝒏πb(𝒏)e−iηB𝒏ρeiηB𝒏=ρ−iη[B‾,ρ]+O(η2),B‾=∑𝒏πb(𝒏)B𝒏=AH𝖥t⊗∑ih‾iPi+AxZ⊗Dx.\begin{gathered} \sum_{\mathbf n}\pi_b(\mathbf n) e^{-i\eta B_{\mathbf n}}\rho e^{i\eta B_{\mathbf n}} =\rho-i\eta[\bar B,\rho]+O(\eta^2),\\ \bar B=\sum_{\mathbf n}\pi_b(\mathbf n)B_{\mathbf n} =A_H\mathsf F_t\otimes\sum_i\bar h_iP_i+A_xZ\otimes D_x. \end{gathered}(S128)

Here the average response comes from the first-order term of the same channel. The next cycle’s entrance is generally correlated and cannot repeatedly be assumed to remain a product. Let ρ(m)=∑𝒏ρ𝒏(m)\rho^{(m)}=\sum_{\mathbf n}\rho_{\mathbf n}^{(m)} after cycle mm, and decompose ρ𝒏(m)=πb(𝒏)ρ(m)+δ𝒏(m)\rho_{\mathbf n}^{(m)}=\pi_b(\mathbf n)\rho^{(m)}+\delta_{\mathbf n}^{(m)}, where ∑𝒏δ𝒏(m)=0\sum_{\mathbf n}\delta_{\mathbf n}^{(m)}=0.

Denote the action of resource transfer on these matrix blocks by 𝒫\mathscr P. Finite mixing ensures ∥𝒫q∥≤Crq\|\mathscr P^q\|\le Cr^q on zero-sum blocks, where 0<r<10<r<1. The first-order expansion of the active stage generates only O(η)O(\eta) correlations per cycle, so starting from δ(0)=0\delta^{(0)}=0 gives

δ(m+1)=𝒫δ(m)+O(η),∥δ(m)∥⊕,1≤C′η∑q=0m−1rq=O(η),∥δ∥⊕,1:=∑𝒏∥δ𝒏∥1.\begin{gathered} \delta^{(m+1)}=\mathscr P\delta^{(m)}+O(\eta),\qquad \|\delta^{(m)}\|_{\oplus,1} \le C'\eta\sum_{q=0}^{m-1}r^q=O(\eta),\\ \|\delta\|_{\oplus,1}:=\sum_{\mathbf n}\|\delta_{\mathbf n}\|_1. \end{gathered}(S129)

After tracing over resources, the zeroth-order correlation term cancels; its contribution to carrier motion in the next cycle acquires another factor η\eta and is therefore O(η2)O(\eta^2). The reduced action differs from the average unitary by O(η2)O(\eta^2) per cycle; summing cycle by cycle using trace-norm invariance under unitary evolution gives the averaging-error bound in equation (4.14) of the main paper. The constants depend on the mixing rate of the fixed resource process and uniform bounds on the norms of the operators used; the actual elapsed duration is NτN\tau. A nonstationary resource entrance additionally has an initial relaxation, and arbitrarily long-time coherent readings still require the complete return channel. Section 4.4.2 of the main paper therefore converts the average generator using the complete cycle period.

S10 Spatial outward and return paths and common response

S10.1 Reception and impulse for complete histories

Let matter position be logical register XX. The source writes occupation at vertex x0=s0x_0=s_0 with probability qs=se/2q_s=se/2. At each step the propagation protocol uses fresh, ready, identically distributed actual edge/idle labels, giving the same Markov transition while retaining orthogonal histories; the outward path reaches x1,…,xmx_1,\ldots,x_m and the return follows the same labels in reverse order to xm−1,…,x0x_{m-1},\ldots,x_0. At the end of each step, target logical position controls local swapping in, readout, and sending back. S11 Approximation regime of nucleon spectral preparation

Section 6.3 of the main paper uses the leading-term prescription β_B=1+1/√3 and complete spectral participation. The comparisons below distinguish prescription choice, spectral cutoff, and the lowest scale within the allowed family.

V(βB)=2.860214657918…,V(βB)−3=−0.139785342081…,V(βB)−33≃−4.6595%.V(\beta_B)=2.860214657918\ldots,\qquad V(\beta_B)-3=-0.139785342081\ldots,\qquad \frac{V(\beta_B)-3}{3}\simeq-4.6595\%.(S141)

This difference cannot be treated as a mass error bar already supplied by the calculation. Replacing the β-selection rule by the exact condition V(β)=3 requires solving for the root and evaluating again, giving β≈1.564273980920, W≈2.388897704196, and M≈962.7840 MeV. The value 936.6693 MeV corresponds to the leading-term condition, and 962.7840 MeV to the exact-variance condition; these are different spectral-preparation prescriptions.

The spectral cutoff is likewise a preparation condition. The main value in 6.3 uses the complete ζ\zeta spectrum; finite participation must instead use ZLZ_L, with errors controlled by the tail bound in S5.3. For example, changing only the participation cutoff to L=2400L=2400 while retaining βB\beta_B, C*C^*, and E0=1E_0=1 GeV gives ZL≃2.330274457513Z_L\simeq2.330274457513 and energy scale 923.7669923.7669 MeV, below the main value by 12.902412.9024 MeV. This illustrates the cutoff effect without imposing the electroweak depth on nucleons; if the background is also truncated, its squared quantity must be replaced simultaneously. The number of operation terms carried by a finite state space also differs from its number of independent states.

Finally, the formal energy scale supplied by the prescribed rule increases strictly with the number n of fundamental color-representation factors. Indeed, β(n) decreases, ζ decreases for β>1, and

ddW(WC*logW)=log⁡W+22C*W>0(W>1),\frac{d}{dW}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac W{C^*}}\log W\right) =\frac{\log W+2}{2\sqrt{C^*W}}>0\qquad(W>1),(S142)

Thus, for pure three-dimensional fundamental color representations, the above β values, and the same energy-scale conditions, n=3 gives the lowest scale in this allowed family. This does not prove exclusion of every decay channel to arbitrarily lower masses, nor turn formal values at n=4,5 into an allowed color-singlet spectrum. Actual excitation, formation, and stability remain determined by the complete process.

S13.4 Common cycle period and mass coefficient

Following the common processing protocol of 2.3, a cycle consists of successive nonoverlapping stages: forward execution UU, output-end maintenance, complete U†U^\dagger, repair, thermal processing, and padded waiting. Matter and background switch on together in the maintenance window and switch off together in the other stages, or complete the specified free-phase compensation. Denote the complete cycle duration and accumulated drives at both endpoints by

T=TU+tH+TU†+Trepair+Tthermal+Tpad,Θν=∫0Tg(t)aν(t)dt,ΘB=∫0Tg(t)aB(t)dt>0,ην=ΘνΘB.\begin{gathered} T=T_U+t_H+T_{U^\dagger}+T_{\mathrm{repair}}+T_{\mathrm{thermal}}+T_{\mathrm{pad}},\\ \Theta_\nu=\int_0^T g(t)a_\nu(t)dt,\qquad \Theta_B=\int_0^T g(t)a_B(t)dt>0,\qquad \eta_\nu=\frac{\Theta_\nu}{\Theta_B}. \end{gathered}(S157)

Simultaneous operations are timed only once; configurations rebuilt every cycle enter the corresponding stages, while one-time setup of a fixed apparatus and initial loading are counted separately. Processing for different thermal outcomes is padded to the same fixed-duration processing interval. Switching these operations is actual control; identical gate types do not automatically imply equal durations.

Finally apply the background squared calibration of (2.77) in the main paper. The common capacity must still satisfy feasibility in S13.1 and the other modules; changing it changes actual preparation and bare frequencies. The mass/background ratio remains unchanged only when both endpoints use the same actual capacity and repeat the common calibration. Increasing processing duration at fixed drive and active window also lowers the actual absolute frequency.

Dividing the same round trip into two calendar cycles introduces no factor of one-half. Only when the accumulated neutral activity is half the background activity does ην=1/2\eta_\nu=1/2 hold; if equal-amplitude ports are still used, both half factors remain. Ports and timing are separately specified in the present common protocol and cannot give two explanations for the same 1/21/2. The common gating and calibration apply consistently to all families; one cannot change only the neutral reference clock while retaining the other families’ old bare frequencies.

This section gives the complete conditional mass matrix of the delivered neutral carrier. With the same ℳ\mathcal M and linear generator retained, the common activity ratio, port flags, and background energy scale change the overall scale; unequal chain weights, the transported object, multiplier coherence, noncommon deformation of the cyclic columns, and finite truncation can change the relative spectrum. Entrance encoding, collective transport, complete return, and simultaneous protection retain their respective physical constructions; ην=1\eta_\nu=1, derived from the common protocol, is no longer listed as a separate neutral-family input. Loading of general incident states, actual decay products, and mixing and oscillations still require their corresponding processes.

S14 Nucleon phase and electromagnetic share

For the complex multiplier aN≠0a_N\ne0 of a complete cycle, write aN/|aN|=eiΘNa_N/|a_N|=e^{i\Theta_N} on a continuously unwrapped phase branch. A share does not determine the sign or point-charge scale. The positive electromagnetic difference of the main text, the scale αEMMB\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}M_B, the depth, and whether address matching here is already included in αEM\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} all retain their original correspondence conditions. This process explanation therefore cannot directly replace the exact 1/61/6 in the main text by a new unconditional value.

For fermionic matter branches ff, take the complete carrier

The natural color representation 𝟑⊕𝟑\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf3 of the original six-dimensional species space does not itself contain a lepton singlet.

The choice r=1r=1 selects the left side, r=−1r=-1 selects the right side, and r=0r=0 accepts both sides equally.

These results establish a conditional selection mechanism for the contact stage. Subsequent original spectral acceptance, label matching, and thermal exit retain their actual outputs. It remains to establish how formation and service processes themselves supply the required oriented reference and shared-contact configuration. This proposition does not identify the conditional selection with a derivation of the complete weak vertex, absolute weak strength, or natural selection of a handedness.

S16 Formation structure and common family returns

The return of a formed carrier includes both formation records and current work auxiliaries. Formation records retain all paths and used work from the initial formation, while current work participates in the present loading, maintenance, and inverse. They enter the complete physical space of the family processes in Chapter 8 as distinct physical factors.

Loading and its inverse preserve coherent reversibility across the success, competitive-failure, parking, tail, and weak-work outputs. Path projectors of the formation record are preserved, coherence between paths evolves with the joint phases, and inverse preparation retrieves the current work. If new attempt outcomes are permanently read out, maintenance compatible with those records is used.

S16.6 Complete timing and physical readings

Initial formation, full-work exchange, and resource supply enter the startup duration. Loading, control, inverse operations, repair, and waiting enter the processing time of each cycle in which they actually occur. With a common active window for mass, background, and motion,

τ=tH+Tproc,fact=tH/τ,mobs=fact|gf|,vE=factgp0Λ.\tau=t_H+T_{\mathrm{proc}},\qquad f_{\mathrm{act}}=t_H/\tau,\qquad m^{\mathrm{obs}}=f_{\mathrm{act}}|gf|,\qquad v_E=\frac{f_{\mathrm{act}}gp_0}{\Lambda}.(S226)

Resource phases are compensated by the actual program or included in the joint generator, with energy–charge compensation, controls, and switching work accounted for in the complete exchanges. The common period cancels the active fraction in mass ratios, while formation and supply probabilities determine branch occupations. Persistent readings here refer to the loaded code subspace; thermal repair and exit follow Section 2.3.6 on their respective domains.

Module inputs and physical attributes follow the correspondence of Chapter 5, while the complete actions in this section specify their paths and endpoints. Down-type and up-type matter each complete their return under a common successor; the charged-lepton and neutral processes are given in Section 8.2 and S13, respectively.
